meta.title: Startup pages, crash recovery and app error pages today

security.label: Step with an evidenced pain point

nodes.label: Open a service URL
nodes.sublabel: a page load in a tab
nodes.explanation: A person opens a service's hostname, alias or path route in a tab. Caddy sends page loads (Sec-Fetch-Dest: document) and devhost's own recovery requests (X-Devhost-Recovery) to the service's document proxy; every other request goes straight to the app's port. devhost never opens a browser.

sources.label: Host route: recovery, page loads, then the app
Only Sec-Fetch-Dest: document is matched

nodes.label: External or daemon page
nodes.explanation: An external service (managed = false) gets the managed-service page unchanged: '<service> is unavailable / The service is not responding. View its logs below and restart it when you are ready.', a Restart <service> button disabled with no reason and a Recent logs box that is always empty, although the docs say external services show their status only and are recovered outside devhost; the Services panel gets this right (manifest-hot-reload-2-04; serve-folder-01 is the same page for devhost serve --port while nothing listens). A daemon that stopped on its own gets 'not responding' too: devhost runs its status command only around a start or a stop, so the page cannot say it stopped, and its logs hold only the start and stop commands' lines (manifest-hot-reload-2-02).

sources.label: Restart only for managed services
Health check only; the managed wording
Restart button always drawn

nodes.label: Starting <service>
nodes.explanation: While the service starts, a page load gets 503 'Starting <service>': 'Waiting for the service to pass its health check. This page will reload when it is ready.' Restart is off. Recent logs are the service's lines from the shared log, so right after a restart they show the previous run's output, and the new run's lines are appended with no divider; the page never shows the health target, the time spent or the timeout that the terminal prints at the same moment (startup-recovery-02). The page polls its status every second; once the service is ready and a probe of the URL gets a non-error answer, the tab reloads itself into the app.

sources.label: Starting <service>; Restart off
Recent logs: one joined block
Ready and probe 204: reload the tab

nodes.label: Failure page: Restart
nodes.explanation: When the start fails, the same tab changes in place to '<service> could not start' (or '<service> exited', '<service> is unavailable') with the cause, 'Service: <name> · <address>', Restart <service>, the checkout picker when worktrees are on, and Recent logs. With the toolbar injected, the toolbar also opens its full-screen 'Service exited' view over this page, because it counts the page's own service: the view drops the stack, the address, the cause sentence and the picker, and once the service's lines leave the log it says only 'No retained logs for this service.' (startup-recovery-01). The page reads '503' before its heading, shows its logs as one unlabeled block with raw ANSI codes, and Restart drops keyboard focus to the page body (keyboard-and-screen-reader-03).

sources.label: could not start / exited titles
Service, address, Restart, error alert
Crash view drawn on any page, status pages too

nodes.label: Document proxy decides
nodes.explanation: Each service has a document proxy. For a page load it asks the stack for the service's state: blocked, starting, failed, exited or not responding returns devhost's 503 page; ready forwards the request to the app and replaces an app 404 or 5xx with devhost's page. API calls, fetches and curl never reach it: before routes exist they get Caddy's 750 KB 404 page even with Accept: application/json, then an empty 502 while the service starts, reloads or has crashed, so starting, crashed and reloading look the same; the JSON status the pages read is behind an undocumented header (agent-cli-journey-04).

sources.label: 503 status page while not ready
Blocked, starting, failed, exited, ready
Replace an app 404 or 5xx page load

nodes.label: Shared 512-line log
nodes.explanation: devhost keeps one 512-line log for the whole stack; the status page's Recent logs and the crash view's log box both read a service's lines from it. A noisy service pushes a crashed service's lines out within minutes, leaving 'could not start' over an empty Recent logs and 'No retained logs for this service.' in the crash view while the terminal still has the stack trace, and neither says lines were dropped (startup-recovery-03). An open crash view also loses lines that arrive together, because each new line replaces the pending list instead of extending it, so the line that says why the service exited can be missing (services-panel-01 and stack-scale-02, duplicates of startup-recovery-03).

sources.label: One 512-entry buffer for every service
Page logs: the service's retained lines
A burst line replaces the pending list

nodes.label: Restart one service
nodes.explanation: Restart <service>, on the status page or in the crash view, asks the stack to restart that one service: devhost stops it and starts it again with the same command, folder and automatic port from the accepted manifest, and answers once the new process passes its health check. The button is disabled while the restart runs.

sources.label: Stop, then start the same service
Page restart: POST; error text as 503
Page Restart calls restart(name)

nodes.label: Restart Stack job
nodes.explanation: Restart Stack stops every managed service, assigns new automatic ports and starts everything again from the last accepted manifest. When one service cannot start, the restart fails, and its restore starts the same service first, fails again and blocks every service it touched: the healthy services stay stopped, every hostname of the stack answers 502, and nothing in the toolbar brings them back (error-pages-01; journey-crash-to-fix-07 is the same outage reached from the crash view). The docs describe a restore of the previous stack.

sources.label: Reapply the accepted manifest, new ports
Failed restore blocks every service

nodes.label: Service exited view
nodes.explanation: When the page's own service, or one it depends on, exits with the app open, the toolbar opens a full-screen modal: 'Service exited / devhost is running. Review the service logs and restart when ready.', '<service> (exit code N)', Restart <service>, a log box, and Restart Stack in the corner. It has no close control and cancels Escape; both buttons rerun the same accepted command, and nothing names the manifest, the command or the folder it ran in, so an error such as 'Module not found "src/server.ts"' cannot be traced (journey-crash-to-fix-01, journey-crash-to-fix-04). The log box opens at the oldest retained line, so the exit cause can sit screens below (stack-scale-03). Its accessible name is only 'Service exited', so a screen reader never hears the cause, and its closing is not announced (keyboard-and-screen-reader-01).

sources.label: Opened as a modal on mount
Escape cancelled; fixed title and line
Log box starts at the oldest line

nodes.label: App 404 or 5xx replaced
nodes.explanation: When the app answers a page load with 404 or 5xx, devhost replaces the app's document with its own page and keeps the status. A framework build error's 500 page hides the framework's own overlay (file, line, code frame) and leads with Restart <service>, which cannot fix code; the cause sits at the bottom of Recent logs, and the advice 'restart after addressing the error' is wrong when the dev server recovers by itself (error-pages-03). An app's own 404 becomes 'Page not found', blaming the checkout, offering Restart for a healthy service and showing neither the requested path nor the app's response (error-pages-04). devhost's own file server's 404 is replaced the same way, losing the folder listing (serve-folder-06). A page load the app drops without answering gets a 502 '<service> could not load' page whose message is Go's raw proxy error after 'The service could not return a document: ' (EOF, connection reset by peer), never saying the service is up or that the page retries (error-pages-07).

sources.label: Any 404 or 5xx page load is replaced
404: checkout wording; 5xx: restart advice
Dropped request: raw Go error as 502

nodes.label: Re-request URL each 1 s
nodes.explanation: The 404 and 5xx pages read their status and then request the same URL every second, with no back-off, no pause in a hidden tab and no end. Each request is a real page load for the dev server, so a failed build is rebuilt and logged again about once a second: the terminal fills with one service's error, the page's own Recent logs repeat it, and other services' lines are pushed out of the shared log (error-pages-05). When a request gets a non-error answer, for example once the code is fixed, the tab reloads into the app.

sources.label: Status, then probe, every 1000 ms
Only a non-error answer passes the probe

nodes.label: Restart fails again
nodes.explanation: A restart that fails leaves the page or the view in place with the error, ready to retry. The command is unchanged, so a broken command fails the same way, and the new attempt's lines run together with the last one's. On the status page the failure is announced twice, as an alert and again in the status line (keyboard-and-screen-reader-03). When another program holds a fixed port, the restart waits 30 s for the health check and blames it, never the port or its holder (error-pages-06; manifest-hot-reload-05 is the same missing port check on hot reload). Only an automatic port gets the error that points to Restart Stack.

sources.label: Automatic port only: use Restart Stack
Error alert while the status line updates
Start failure logged and returned

nodes.label: Stack down, view gone
nodes.explanation: After a failed Restart Stack the crash view closes: it leaves out services whose checkout carries an error, and the failed restore stored its error on every checkout. Its 'Stack restart failed' message lived inside the view, so no toast, notice or panel says anything while the whole stack is down; the only trace is 'attention required' on the Worktrees trigger, and the Services panel shows a 13-line block that repeats one sentence (error-pages-02).

sources.label: View skips services of a failed checkout
Blocked reason stored on the checkout
Error kept in the view's own button

nodes.label: Service exits, app open
nodes.explanation: The page's own service, or a service it lists in dependsOn, directly or through another service, exits while the app is open. Any other service that exits only turns red in the Services panel, so a Storybook crash does not cover the app.

sources.label: The page's service and its dependencies

nodes.label: The app loads again
nodes.explanation: The tab shows the app again at the same URL: a status page reloads itself once the service is ready and a probe gets a non-error answer, and the crash view closes once the service is healthy (on devhost's own status pages it reloads them).

sources.label: Reload once the probe answers 204
View restart; reload on status pages

cards.title: What already works
items: A failed service leaves the rest of the stack running, and its hostname, every alias and path route, shows what went wrong
Status pages need nothing from the app and still show the error, service details and logs without JavaScript
The tab reloads itself at the same URL once the service is healthy; devhost never opens a browser
Restart <service> keeps the automatic port, succeeds only once the new process is healthy, and can be retried
Replaced 404 and 5xx pages keep the app's status code and are never cached; API calls, assets and WebSockets get the app's own response
An exit elsewhere in the stack (a Storybook crash) never covers the app; only the page's service and its dependencies open the crash view

cards.title: Tickets on this journey
items: error-pages-01 Restart Stack with one service that cannot start stops every healthy service and leaves the stack down (journey-crash-to-fix-07, duplicate)
error-pages-02 A failed Restart Stack closes the crash view; no error appears anywhere while the stack is down
error-pages-03 A build error's 500 page hides the framework's overlay and leads with Restart, which cannot fix code
startup-recovery-03 A crashed service's lines leave the shared 512-line log, and the open crash view drops burst lines (services-panel-01 and stack-scale-02, duplicates)
startup-recovery-01 The toolbar's crash view opens over the failure page and hides its cause, address and checkout picker
startup-recovery-02 Startup and failure pages mix earlier runs' output and show no health-check progress
journey-crash-to-fix-01 The crash view is a dead end: modal, Escape blocked, both buttons rerun the broken command
journey-crash-to-fix-04 Nothing shows the command, folder or manifest line behind an error
stack-scale-03 The crash view's log box opens at the oldest line, screens above the exit cause
keyboard-and-screen-reader-01 The crash view's accessible name never carries the cause, and its closing is not announced
keyboard-and-screen-reader-03 Status pages read '503' first, announce a failed restart twice and present logs as one raw block
error-pages-04 An app's own 404 blames the checkout and offers Restart for a healthy service
error-pages-05 404 and 5xx pages request the URL every second with no end, flooding the logs
serve-folder-06 A 404 from devhost's own file server is replaced by the service recovery page
manifest-hot-reload-2-04 An external service's page offers empty logs and a disabled Restart (serve-folder-01, duplicate)
manifest-hot-reload-2-02 A daemon that stopped on its own is only 'not responding', with its start and stop lines as logs
agent-cli-journey-04 API calls get 750 KB of 404 HTML, then empty 502s, while a service starts, reloads or has crashed
error-pages-06 A fixed port held by another program fails a restart after 30 s and blames the health check (manifest-hot-reload-05)
error-pages-07 A page load the app drops gets a 502 page with Go's raw proxy error, never saying the service is up or that it retries
